title: Choose System Boundaries and Data Ownership
summary: Decide which system owns each fact, how other systems use it, and what happens when they disagree.
prerequisites: Understand REST integration, asynchronous events, and batch processing.
Know Northstar's vehicle, client, and appointment records.
learningObjectives: Distinguish a system of record from a copied view.
Choose interaction patterns using latency and consistency requirements.
Define reconciliation before promising reliable integration.

sections.heading: One business process can have several authoritative systems
body: Northstar uses Salesforce for customer interactions, a dealer management system for workshop operations, and a stock service for vehicle availability. A system of record is the authoritative source for a particular fact. It does not have to own every field about an entity. Salesforce may own the requested appointment while the scheduling system owns the confirmed workshop slot.

Make ownership precise at the field or decision level. If both systems can independently declare the same slot reserved, a conflict policy is required. Copying the value into Salesforce does not transfer authority. Distinguish the authoritative state from a cached or replicated view, and show when the view was last refreshed.

callouts.text: Ask who is allowed to decide a fact, not only which system happens to store a copy.

sections.heading: Match the pattern to the business promise
body: A synchronous request asks another system for an answer while the caller waits. It fits a decision that requires a current authoritative result, but introduces a dependency into the user's critical path. An asynchronous message decouples timing, but the interface must communicate pending work and eventual outcomes. Batch synchronization moves a set of changes periodically; it can suit information whose freshness tolerance is larger.

Virtual access reads information without necessarily maintaining a full local copy. It can reduce duplication, but availability, query support, performance, authorization, and product licensing must fit the use case. It is not automatically simpler just because less data is stored locally.

The synthetic decisions below illustrate differing freshness needs. They are proposed requirements to discuss with Oleg, not defaults imposed by Salesforce. If the business later says availability must be confirmed atomically with reservation, a display-only stock feed is insufficient. You need a reservation contract with the authoritative system.

callouts.text: State the acceptable age of a value and the behavior when its source is unavailable.

codeBlocks.caption: Synthetic data-ownership worksheet
codeBlocks.code:
Client contact preference: Salesforce owns; changes sent to permitted consumers
Vehicle stock state: stock service owns; Salesforce displays a dated view
Requested test-drive: Salesforce owns the request
Confirmed slot: scheduling service owns the reservation decision
Monthly dealer summary: derived report; refresh tolerance agreed with Oleg
Open issue: whether booking requires synchronous reservation or may remain Pending

sections.heading: Design the failure contract with the success contract
body: Suppose Anna saves a request but the scheduling service is unavailable. If the approved process allows Pending, show that state and retain a recoverable work item. Do not display Confirmed simply because a message was enqueued. If the process requires immediate confirmation, return an understandable failure or an explicitly permitted alternative instead of inventing a reservation.

Pending is a user-facing integration state in this scenario, not a value already present in the starter picklist. The starter Test_Drive__c.Status__c values are Requested, Confirmed, Completed, and Cancelled. Keep an unconfirmed request as Requested and define a separate integration-state field if the implementation needs finer detail. Document any new metadata and map source states deliberately before writing them.

Reconciliation compares systems to find missing or inconsistent work. Define the business key, expected state, comparison frequency, responsible operator, and permitted repair. A message stream alone is not a permanent record of every business decision. A long outage or a consumer defect can require rebuilding state from an authoritative source.

Prevent an update loop. If Salesforce publishes a change, the DMS echoes it, and Salesforce republishes it as a new local decision, the systems can generate endless work. Use explicit source identity, operation identity, and ownership rules. Do not solve the problem by indiscriminately ignoring every inbound update.

callouts.text: For each integration arrow, write who initiates it, what outcome it promises, and how an unresolved outcome is found.

sections.heading: Keep the first implementation narrow
body: Begin with one field-level ownership map and one complete business journey. A small mock service can return Available, Unavailable, Timeout, and an existing reservation for a repeated key. This tests the application's reaction without requiring a real DMS or an industry product license.

Measure user-visible wait for synchronous dependencies and pending-work age for asynchronous ones. Count unresolved mismatches in reconciliation. These metrics answer different questions; a low API error count can coexist with many appointments stuck Pending because a consumer stopped processing.

Do not copy all DMS data into Salesforce because a future use might exist. Every copy brings storage, privacy, freshness, mapping, and support responsibilities. On the other hand, a carefully chosen local view may be justified when staff need to continue working through a brief dependency outage. Explain the tradeoff rather than adopting 'never copy' as another absolute rule.

callouts.text: An integration diagram without data ownership and failure behavior is incomplete, even when every arrow names an API.

exercise.title: Choose five Northstar integration patterns
exercise.brief: Complete the ownership worksheet and choose an interaction pattern for each fact.
steps: Name the authoritative owner, allowed writers, consumer, and stable business key for each row.
State freshness tolerance and what Anna sees during a source outage.
Choose synchronous request, asynchronous message, scheduled synchronization, or supported virtual access with a reason.
Design one reconciliation check and one loop-prevention rule.
Use a mock response table to walk through successful reservation, timeout, duplicate request, and unavailable slot.
acceptance: A copy is never mistaken for the authoritative decision.
The user-facing status matches the actual confirmation guarantee.
Each asynchronous or replicated flow has a way to find and resolve missing work.
exercise.stretch: Explain how the design changes if Oleg requires booking during a DMS outage.

knowledgeCheck.question: Must one system own every field of an entity?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. Authority can be divided by fact or decision, provided the write rules and conflict behavior are explicit.

knowledgeCheck.question: What does an asynchronous acceptance prove?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It proves only the stage defined by its contract, often that work was accepted or queued; it does not automatically prove downstream completion.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why design reconciliation if events are already used?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Events can be missed, mishandled, or unavailable after retention. Reconciliation compares durable business state and repairs unresolved differences.

recap: Assign authority before choosing a transport.
Match consistency and freshness to the business promise.
Define recovery and reconciliation on every important boundary.

illustration.prompt: Create one landscape 16:9 lesson-cover illustration for SAM Salesforce Developer Studio. Restrained professional editorial illustration, flat geometric drawn forms with fine navy linework and a subtle paper texture. Warm ivory #F7F4EE, navy #12253C, muted cobalt #3867E8, restrained teal #138A86 and sage. One clear central scene, generous empty margins, at most three main visual groups. Calm adult learning design. Any people are clearly drawn stylized figures, never realistic photos. NO text, letters, numerals, logos, watermarks, Salesforce mascots, decorative clutter or glossy 3D. Exact topic: System Ownership. Subject: two systems with one record clearly owned by one system and a controlled synchronisation path.
